findings.finding: Claim under doubt: greenfield /shipwright-project always writes AGENTS.md unconditionally (mini-plan decision 2) — SKILL.md Step 7/8 and two of its own reference/checkpoint files (step-7-scaffolding.md, step-8-completion.md) were not updated in the original diff and still enumerated only CLAUDE.md in their Goal line, Key sub-flows list, Checkpoint line, Verification checklist, and completion banner — an agent following those surfaces as the authoritative TODO had no textual cue that AGENTS.md needed to exist, and nothing code-level gates on its presence.

Claim under doubt: the Codex appendix append is idempotent — a second/third/fourth adopt run never duplicates content — The marker check is decoupled from the visible heading, but an existing AGENTS.md whose content matches the appendix bytes yet is missing the marker line (e.g. a hand-copy of the rendered view, which visually hides HTML comments, or a markdown formatter stripping comments) would receive a full duplicate append on the next adopt run.
findings.suggestion: A content-similarity secondary check, or an explicit written acceptance that a marker-stripped hand-copy producing a visible duplicate is an acceptable, narrow edge case

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: AGENTS.md's shared body cannot drift from CLAUDE.md's despite being rendered by a single shared function (the 'single-source guarantee') — This is code-enforced for the brownfield (adopt) path, but NOT for the greenfield (/shipwright-project) path: project-scaffolding.md asks the LLM agent to perform two manual find/replace substitutions inside fully-filled prose (harder than isolated-token substitution), and the only automated check verified the instruction FILE names the right appendix path, not that any scaffolded project's actual output received both substitutions correctly.
findings.suggestion: Either accept as a known, slightly-increased risk, or add a lightweight check that the two substitutions are mechanically well-defined

findings.finding: The spec explicitly required generalizing `is_loadbearing_claude_md` to take a filename/rel_path parameter — "thread the filename explicitly through the whole chain rather than leaving any CLAUDE.md-specific name/key hardcoded" (plan-review round 1, openai medium). The diff instead aliases the CLAUDE.md-named function and reuses it for AGENTS.md. Behaviorally equivalent (the function only checks byte size of the path it's given), so this is a documented-deviation issue, not a bug.
findings.suggestion: Either rename to `is_loadbearing_doc` with a `rel_path`-style parameter as the spec asked, or note the deviation in the preservation_log/commit message so the accepted plan-review finding is traceable.

findings.finding: CODEX_APPENDIX_MARKER` is a hardcoded constant in Python and embedded as the appendix file's first line — two copies that can desync. If someone edits the appendix's first-line comment, `_append_codex_appendix` would stack a duplicate appendix on every adopt re-run. The comment claims "reading the appendix and checking for the marker can never desync", which is only true because the test `test_codex_appendix_marker_is_embedded_in_the_live_file` pins it — the guard is the test, not the construction.
findings.suggestion: Consider deriving the marker at runtime (e.g. read the appendix's first line when appending) or at least keep the test; it exists, so this is acceptable as-is.

findings.finding: assert "demo" in body` is a weak signal — it passes on almost any rendered content (project name "Demo" lowercase, profile slug, product_description) and would pass even if the overwrite wrote stale/wrong content as long as it contained "demo". The sibling CLAUDE.md tests presumably assert more.
findings.suggestion: Assert a load-bearing fragment of the rendered body (e.g. `# Demo` heading and `Codex withholds subagent spawning`) instead of a bare substring.

findings.finding: The heading-presence check is `^` + literal heading prefix. For the standing-request heading (`## Review subagents: standing request.`), a preserved file containing that text at a line start inside a fenced code block would still be treated as present. The docstring claims line-anchoring fixes the fenced-block false positive, but it only fixes mid-line matches, not fenced blocks. Same false-negative risk existed before, so not a regression; just overstated in the comment.
findings.suggestion: Either accept it (matches prior behavior for CLAUDE.md) or strip fenced blocks before the check; at minimum soften the docstring claim.

findings.finding: Spec design §2 places `write_agents_md` inside `claude_md_renderer.py`; the diff moves it to a new module citing a 300-line source cap. The hooks doc and tests are consistent with the new location, and the import wiring (`sys.path` insert + `from lib.claude_md_renderer import ...`) is correct, so this is a benign, documented deviation.
findings.suggestion: None needed; just confirming it isn't an orphaned file.

findings.finding: _append_section_if_missing` treats any line-start occurrence as an existing section, including one inside a fenced Markdown code block. A preserved, load-bearing `AGENTS.md` containing an example of `<!-- shipwright:codex-agents-md-appendix -->` or the standing-request heading in a code fence will not receive the real appendix and/or standing request, violating the required preserved-file delivery behavior.
findings.suggestion: Detect headings/markers only outside fenced code blocks (and preferably match complete heading lines). Add preserved-AGENTS tests containing the marker and standing-request heading inside fenced code examples.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation largely follows the requested shared-body and appendix design, but the idempotency check can silently omit required Codex guidance for valid existing project documentation.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
